"""Approximate a mostly negative response to Python-looking code.

Rules use Python builtins, module and array/table API names, member-access
spellings and common package names. A decaying cue from explicit Python syntax strengthens
responses to ambiguous words, assignments, imports, brackets and indentation.
Names split across tokens are joined in a short tail; document changes reset it.
Repeated middle-dot tokens have a separate positive response. This is a spelling
heuristic, not a parser or an exact account of individual API names.
"""
import re, sys, keyword, builtins
from functools import lru_cache
import numpy as np

BUILTINS = set(dir(builtins))
GENERAL = {'abs','all','any','max','min','sum','range','round','pow',
           'type','object','help'}
API = set(sys.stdlib_module_names) | set(dir(np.ndarray))
API |= {'DataFrame','Series','Index'}
PACKAGES = {'np','numpy','pd','pandas','plt','matplotlib','scipy','sklearn',
            'torch','tensorflow','tf','pytest','requests','django','flask',
            'pygame','pydantic','setuptools','pylint','sympy','scrapy',
            'jupyter','qiskit','seaborn','sphinx'}
SEMANTIC = {'builtin','general_builtin','exception','literal','self','kwargs',
            'python','package','api'}

BLOCK_HEAD = re.compile(
    r'\b(if|elif|else|for|while|def|try|except|finally|class|with)\b[^\n]*$'
)

@lru_cache(None)
def category(t):
    s=t.strip()
    if not s:
        return 'indent' if '\n' not in t and len(t)>=3 else 'space'
    if len(s)>1 and set(s)=={'·'}: return 'middle_dot'
    if s=='.py': return 'python'
    if s in {'(**','(*'}: return 'unpack'
    if s.startswith(('/_','._')) or s in {'_','__','__('}: return 'private'
    if s=='(f': return 'f_argument'
    if s=='=': return 'assign'
    if re.fullmatch(r'[+*/%&|^-]=|[<>=!]=|[<>]',s): return 'operator'
    if (s.endswith(':') and '\n' in t) or s.endswith(':\\'):
        return 'paragraph_colon' if t.count('\n')>1 else 'colon_line'
    if re.fullmatch(r'["\']:',s): return 'json_colon'
    if re.fullmatch(r'[\[({]+[\'\"]?',s): return 'open'
    # Names may share a token with an opening delimiter or assignment.
    w=s.lstrip('._([,=').rstrip('(')
    if w=='kwargs': return 'kwargs'
    if w in {'f','r','b','u'}: return 'string_prefix'
    if w.lower() in {'py','python'}: return 'python'
    if w in {'self','cls'}: return 'self'
    if w in {'None','True','False'}: return 'literal'
    if w=='import': return 'import'
    if w in {'return','yield','raise','assert','del','pass','break','continue'}:
        return 'statement'
    if w in keyword.kwlist: return 'keyword'
    if w in BUILTINS:
        if w.endswith(('Error','Exception')): return 'exception'
        return 'general_builtin' if w in GENERAL else 'builtin'
    if w in PACKAGES: return 'package'
    if w in API or (s.startswith('.') and w.isidentifier()): return 'api'
    if s.startswith('(') and w.isidentifier(): return 'open'
    if s.isdigit(): return 'number'
    if (s in {',',';',':','::','"',"'",'`'}
            or re.fullmatch(r'[\])}]+[,:;]?',s)):
        return 'punctuation'
    return 'word'


def advance(state,t):
    confidence, tail = state if state is not None else (0.,'')
    s=t.strip(); c=category(t); joined=tail+t
    if t=='n' and tail.endswith('\\'): c='escaped_newline'
    m=re.search(r'[A-Za-z_]\w*$',joined)
    if m and s and not t[0].isspace() and not s.startswith('.'):
        w=m.group(); wc=category(w)
        if c in ({'word'} | SEMANTIC) and wc in SEMANTIC: c=wc
        elif c in SEMANTIC and wc not in SEMANTIC and w!=s: c='word'
        if w.startswith('__') and len(w)>2: c='private'
    confidence *= .95
    if c in {'self','package','python','kwargs'} or s in {'def','lambda','(**'}:
        confidence=max(confidence,.98)
    if s.startswith(('/_','._')) or re.search(r'[)\]]:',s):
        confidence=max(confidence,.98)
    if s=='**' and re.search(r'[(,] *$',tail):
        c='unpack'; confidence=max(confidence,.98)
    if c=='colon_line' and BLOCK_HEAD.search(tail):
        confidence=max(confidence,.9)
    if re.search(r'\bfor\s+[A-Za-z_]\w*\s+in$',joined):
        confidence=max(confidence,.9)
    if s in {'from','print'} and re.search(r'(?:^|\n)[ \t]*$',tail):
        confidence=max(confidence,.9 if s=='from' else .8)
        if s=='from': c='import'
    if c=='assign':
        m=re.search(r'(?:^|\n)[ \t]*([a-z_]\w*(?:\.[A-Za-z_]\w*)*) *$',tail)
        if m and len(m.group(1))>1: confidence=max(confidence,.5)
    return (confidence,joined.replace('\\n','\n')[-160:]),c,confidence

READS = ()

# Fixed responses, or (baseline, adjustment times recent Python-cue strength).
RESPONSE = {
    'api': (-0.02, -0.812),
    'assign': (-0.028, -1.821),
    'builtin': (-0.059, -1.25),
    'colon_line': (0.003, -1.191),
    'escaped_newline': (-0.049, -0.684),
    'exception': (-0.983, -1.179),
    'f_argument': (-0.763, -2.629),
    'general_builtin': (-0.017, -0.928),
    'import': (-0.015, -1.682),
    'indent': (-0.013, -0.382),
    'json_colon': (-0.458, -0.61),
    'keyword': (0.006, -0.642),
    'kwargs': -3.13,
    'literal': (-0.81, -0.342),
    'middle_dot': 1.174,
    'number': (-0.002, -0.028),
    'open': (0.003, -0.556),
    'operator': (0.011, -0.47),
    'package': -1.194,
    'paragraph_colon': (-0.02, -0.249),
    'private': (-0.099, -0.97),
    'punctuation': (0.002, -0.179),
    'python': -1.021,
    'self': -0.685,
    'space': (-0.0, -0.064),
    'statement': (-0.088, -1.37),
    'string_prefix': (-0.024, -0.547),
    'unpack': (-0.263, -1.465),
    'word': (-0.001, -0.19),
}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    state = carry[1] if carry is not None and carry[0] == doc else None
    state, kind, confidence = advance(state, prefix.token_strings[-1])
    response = RESPONSE[kind]
    if isinstance(response, tuple):
        baseline, adjustment = response
        response = baseline + adjustment * confidence
    return (doc, state), float(response)

   <|endoftext|>), which gives a fixed -1.8 because at a document start the

(std about 0.05 per token) that no short rule captures.

intensifier frame and so are followed by an evaluative or quantified noun
phrase:

  - "a bit of a", "much of a", "something of a",
    "kind of a", "more of a"                            (~7)
  - "too small a", "as great a", "so rigid a",

              "long", "short", "broad", "narrow", "wide", "deep", "heavy", "light", "rigid",
              "vague", "dark", "bright", "hard", "easy", "difficult", "simple", "serious", "nice",
              "fine", "fair", "rare", "odd", "strange", "close", "clear", "precarious",
              "scientific", "green", "biting", "new", "old", "tall", "fast", "slow", "thick",
              "thin", "sharp", "cheap", "rich", "poor", "happy", "brave", "bold", "clever",
              "smart", "funny", "lovely", "beautiful", "important", "interesting", "huge",
              "tiny", "massive", "enormous", "pretty", "ugly", "common", "unusual", "remarkable"}

INDONESIAN_WORDS = frozenset(
    """yang dan ini itu untuk dengan tidak dari dalam pada akan oleh bisa sudah juga karena atau
    adalah saya kami kita mereka dapat telah tersebut para hanya lebih serta secara sebagai ada
    anda dia tak belum harus masih sangat banyak setiap pun lah kan nya saat ketika jika jadi
    bahwa seperti antara hingga sampai bagi kepada terhadap namun tetapi kemudian selama sehingga
    bukan begitu orang tahun hari mau ingin memang tentang bagaimana siapa mengapa menjadi
    memiliki melakukan dilakukan akibat bersama masyarakat pemerintah indonesia sebuah suatu
    beberapa semua baru kali lagi pernah masing""".split()
)

# Typical activation of each verb-prefix fragment inside Indonesian text.
PREFIX_ACTIVATION = {
    # meN- (the nasal prefix): me-, mem-, men-, meng-, meny-, mel-, ...
    "meng": -10.0, "meny": -10.0, "mem": -10.0, "menc": -10.0, "men": -9.0, "mer": -9.0,
    "memb": -8.0, "mend": -8.0, "mel": -8.0, "menj": -7.0,
    # di- (passive / verb prefix): di, dip, dib, dit, did, dis, dik, dil, dir, dim, dig, din
    "dip": -10.0, "dib": -10.0, "did": -10.0, "dit": -10.0, "dik": -7.0, "dil": -7.0,
    "dir": -6.0, "dis": -6.0, "dim": -6.0, "dig": -6.0, "din": -6.0, "di": -6.0, "d": -3.0,
    # peN- (noun/verb prefix): pem-, pemb-, peng-, penc-, peny-, pen-, pend-, pel-
    "penc": -8.0, "peny": -7.0, "peng": -5.0, "pemb": -4.0, "pem": -4.0, "pend": -4.0,
    # fragments of prefixed words split mid-word (di-per-lukan, pe-meriksa, me-ncegah)
    "iper": -5.0, "emer": -4.0, "ence": -6.0,
    "pen": -4.0, "pent": -3.0, "pel": -2.0,
}

WINDOW = 40  # previous words of the same document that set the Indonesian strength


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    document = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    word = prefix.token_strings[-1].strip().lower()
    recent = [] if carry is None or carry[0] != document else carry[1]

    # 0 with no Indonesian function words among the recent words, 1 with three or more.
    strength = min(sum(w in INDONESIAN_WORDS for w in recent) / 3.0, 1.0)

    value = 0.0
    if word in PREFIX_ACTIVATION:
        value = PREFIX_ACTIVATION[word] * strength
    elif word == "ی" and recent and recent[-1] == "م":
        value = -7.0  # Persian mi- prefix, written as م then ی

    recent = (recent + [word])[-WINDOW:]
    return (document, recent), float(value)

"""Layer 1 MLP down-projection, component 1462: the indefinite-article detector.

It fires on the word "a" / "an" (and on the other indefinite determiners "some",
"another", "something", "un/une/ein/eine/una/egy", "few", "little") -- the words that open
an indefinite noun phrase whose referent is new. Capitalised "A"/"An" at a sentence start
fire more weakly. "such a" is the exception: there the article points to a degree
("such a long..."), and the component goes negative. It also fires on "of" right after a
quantity noun ("a cup of", "a couple of"), where the next words will again be an
indefinite phrase.

Its activation is a fixed value per word type, not a function of the context beyond the
one previous word. A repeated middle-dot filler ("··") gives a strong negative value; this
is rare, from one degenerate document in the sample.

Everything else predicts 0. The small residual variance on other tokens is diffuse and is
not modelled.
"""

READS = ()

# Indefinite articles in the usual lowercase, space-prefixed form.
ARTICLES = {" a", " an"}
# Other indefinite determiners and quantifiers; they fire somewhat less.
OTHER_INDEFINITES = {
    " some", " another", " something", " someone", " few", " little",
    " un", " une", " ein", " eine", " einer", " einem", " einen",
    " una", " uma", " um", " egy", " một",
}
# Capitalised article forms, typically at the start of a sentence.
CAPITALISED_ARTICLES = {" A", " An", "A", "An"}
# Nouns of quantity, after which "of" starts a partitive phrase ("a cup of tea").
QUANTITY_NOUNS = {
    " couple", " cup", " piece", " bunch", " lot", " lots", " set", " suite", " sheet",
    " snippet", " handful", " bit", " series", " glass", " array", " sketch", " slice", " pair",
}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    """Activation at the newest token, from that token and the one before it."""
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    previous = prefix.token_strings[-2] if len(prefix.token_strings) > 1 else ""
    if token in ARTICLES:
        # "such a" points to a degree, not a new referent: the component goes negative.
        return None, -0.5 if previous == " such" else 0.9
    if token in OTHER_INDEFINITES:
        return None, 0.6
    if token in CAPITALISED_ARTICLES:
        return None, 0.3
    if token == " of" and previous in QUANTITY_NOUNS:
        return None, 0.6
    if token == "··":
        return None, -1.4
    return None, 0.0

"""layers.1.mlp.down_proj:1464 -- a rough reader of "be"-verbs and digit "2".

What the component does (as far as a short rule set can say):
  * It is mostly near zero, with rare, sharp positive peaks on two things:
      - the digit "2" written right after another digit, strongest after "1"
        ("12", "112", "2012" ...): about +0.2 on "12", smaller after 3, 5, 7, 9.
      - a "be"-verb that heads a passive or passive-like phrase:
        "is being" / "are being" / "was being" (about +0.6), "can (then/easily/
        only) be" (about +0.25), "is/need/has to be" (about +0.35).
        "be" after linking or raising verbs ("seems to be", "found to be",
        "appears to be", "going to be") is slightly negative.
  * At the first token of a document (after a document break, or at the row
    start) its value depends only on that token: it is negative for most
    words and capitalised openers, strongly negative for prepositions
    ("of", "to", "in" ...), and positive for digits, commas and "a".
    Those first tokens carry about a fifth of its variance.

Everything else is predicted as 0. The rules are a readable summary, not a full
account: a per-token lookup table would explain more variance, but these rules
keep the concepts visible.

The program keeps no state: each position is judged from the token and the one
or two tokens before it, and from whether it starts a document.
"""

READS = ()

DIGITS = set("0123456789")
# first tokens of a document that push the component negative / positive
PREPOSITIONS = {" of", " to", " in", " for", " by", " from", " at", " on", " into",
                " with", " between", " as", " that"}
POSITIVE_OPENERS = {",", " a", " the", " and", "#", "import"}
# auxiliaries that make a following "being" passive-progressive
COPULA = {" is", " are", " was", " were", " be", " been"}
# words before "to be" that make it a passive/need-type "to be"
PASSIVE_TO_BE = {" is", " are", " was", " were", " need", " needs", " has", " had", " have"}
# words before "to be" that make it a linking/raising "to be" (negative)
LINKING_TO_BE = {" seem", " seems", " seemed", " appear", " appears", " appeared", " found",
                 " consider", " considered", " likely", " expected", " supposed", " going",
                 " tend", " want", " wants", " wanted"}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    tok = prefix.token_strings[-1]

    # First token of a document (or of the row): depends on the token alone.
    if prefix.position == 0 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]:
        if tok in DIGITS:
            return None, 0.17
        if tok in POSITIVE_OPENERS:
            return None, 0.25
        if tok in PREPOSITIONS:
            return None, -0.4
        if tok.strip()[:1].isupper():
            return None, -0.25
        return None, -0.13

    prev = prefix.token_strings[-2]
    prev2 = prefix.token_strings[-3] if prefix.position >= 2 else ""

    if tok == "2":
        if prev == "1":
            return None, 0.21
        if prev in DIGITS:
            return None, 0.08
        return None, 0.0

    if tok == " being":
        return None, 0.55 if prev in COPULA else 0.05

    if tok == " be":
        if prev == " to":
            if prev2 in LINKING_TO_BE:
                return None, -0.1
            if prev2 in PASSIVE_TO_BE:
                return None, 0.35
            return None, 0.05
        if prev in {" can", " then", " easily", " only"}:
            return None, 0.25
        return None, 0.0

    return None, 0.0

"""Component layers.1.mlp.down_proj:1465 as a word detector for "manage".

What it does, in plain terms: it lights up on the letters "manag" when they finish a word
in the current token. Predicted activations, by the word the token completes:

  management, manage, managing, Management ... about +6
  managed, manages                              about +3.5
  manager (singular, e.g. "Manager", " manager") about +1.5
  mgr (as in "_mgr")                            about +4
  Chinese 管理 ("manage/management")            about +3.5

It also fires when "manag" is completed across two tokens (e.g. "studentman" + "agers",
"MAN" + "AGER"). Right after "managed" or "manages", the next token " to" is pushed
negative, about -4. Everything else is 0.

The main program is `step`: it keeps the last 12 characters of the current document's text
(lower-cased) as its carry, so it reads only the newest token, and it resets at a document
boundary. Values are hand-set means from a sample of about 500k training tokens.
"""

import re

READS = ()

WIDTH = 12  # characters of text carried from one position to the next


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    tail = carry or ""
    if len(prefix.document_ids) > 1 and prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]:
        tail = ""
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    word = token.lower()
    text = tail + word
    value = 0.0
    if "manag" in text and "manag" not in tail:
        # this token completes "manag": pick a strength from the word it finishes
        if re.search(r"manager$", text):
            value = 1.5
        elif re.search(r"manag(ed|es)$", text):
            value = 3.5
        else:
            value = 6.0
    elif "mgr" in word:
        value = 4.0
    elif "管理" in token:
        value = 3.5
    elif token.strip() == "to" and re.search(r"manag(ed|es)$", tail):
        value = -4.0
    return text[-WIDTH:], value

"""layers.1.mlp.down_proj:1466 -- the word "say".

This component is a lexical detector for the verb "say". It switches on at the
token that completes an inflected form of "say" in running text: " said",
" say", " says", " saying", "Say", and the archaic "saith". It also responds,
more weakly, to the same verb in some other languages and spellings (German
"sagt"/"sagen", Swedish "säga"/"sä", Danish/Norwegian "siger"). It stays at
about zero on other speech verbs ("told", "stated", "according"), on other
"sa..." words ("sample", "safe", "same") and on everything else.

The program reads the word being typed: it keeps the letters of the current
word in `carry` (reset at each document start), and it predicts a fixed
activation when that word is one of the forms above.
"""

import re

READS = ()

# English forms of "say", and the activation they typically produce.
SAY_FORMS = {"say": 4.8, "said": 4.5, "says": 4.1, "saying": 5.1, "saith": 6.8}

# Same verb in other languages / spellings: weaker, less consistent.
COGNATES = {"sagt": 3.0, "sagen": 3.0, "sag": 3.0, "sade": 3.0, "sä": 3.0,
            "säga": 3.0, "säger": 3.0, "sägen": 3.0, "siger": 3.0}

TABLE = {**SAY_FORMS, **COGNATES}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    # carry: the letters of the word being typed so far ("" at a document start)
    new_doc = len(prefix.document_ids) < 2 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]
    word = "" if carry is None or new_doc else carry
    # Extend the current word with this token's trailing letters (a space or punctuation ends it).
    word = re.search(r"[^\W\d_]*$", (word + prefix.token_strings[-1]).lower()).group(0)
    return word, float(TABLE.get(word, 0.0))

"""Layer-1 MLP neuron 1467 (the down_proj component `layers.1.mlp.down_proj:1467`).

What it does, in plain terms: it is a small, sparse feature that is mostly quiet. It
switches on in three kinds of text:

* Import statements in Java, Android and Python code. On the package segment that follows
  the root name (`import java.util`, `import android.view`, `import org.springframework.web`)
  it goes positive, and on the ` as` in `import numpy as np` or `import pandas as pd`.
* `@example` in placeholder e-mail addresses (`name@example.com`).
* Structured "label: value" text. The colon that closes a field label (`warning:`,
  `Error:`, `Posts:`, `Date:`) goes clearly negative, and any other colon goes slightly
  negative. A `{` right after `\\begin` (LaTeX environments) goes negative too.

Everything else predicts 0. The values are rough averages seen in training text, not a
fitted model. The program keeps the current line in its carry, to know whether it is
inside an import line.
"""

READS = ()

# Common package segments after a root name in Java / Android / Spring imports.
PACKAGE_SEGMENTS = {
    ".util", ".view", ".web", ".data", ".annotation", ".app", ".os", ".widget", ".io",
    ".net", ".support", ".beans", ".stereotype", ".model", ".text", ".lang", ".awt",
    ".sql", ".swing", ".math", ".stream", ".concurrent", ".servlet", ".bind", ".factory",
    ".domain", ".ui", ".content", ".graphics", ".media", ".View", ".Log",
}

# Words that name a field in "Label: value" text.
FIELD_LABELS = {
    "warning", "error", "errors", "posts", "time", "date", "name", "value", "id", "pass",
    "fail", "directory", "views", "replies", "posted", "title", "question", "note",
}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    tok = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    prev = prefix.token_strings[-2] if len(prefix.token_strings) > 1 else ""
    new_doc = len(prefix.token_strings) == 1 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]
    line = "" if (new_doc or carry is None) else carry  # text of this line before tok
    stripped = line.lstrip()
    in_import = stripped.startswith("import ") or stripped.startswith("from ")
    first_dot = "." not in line  # no dot yet on this line: tok is the segment after the root

    value = 0.0
    if tok == ":":
        if prev.strip().lower() in FIELD_LABELS:
            value = -0.5
        elif prev.strip()[:1].isupper():
            value = -0.2
        else:
            value = -0.12
    elif tok == "{" and prev == "begin":
        value = -1.1
    elif tok == "package" and not line.strip():
        value = -0.5
    elif tok == "@example":
        value = 1.8
    elif in_import and tok == " as":
        value = 1.4
    elif in_import and first_dot and tok in PACKAGE_SEGMENTS:
        value = 1.3

    next_carry = tok.split("\n")[-1] if "\n" in tok else line + tok
    return next_carry, value

"""layers.1.mlp.down_proj:1468: a sparse component that fires on Chinese words of sharing,
mutual benefit and self-reliance.

Its activation is near zero on almost every token (std about 0.05). On a few tokens it is
large: about +1 to +6 on the second half of compound words built on the bound morphemes
共 (together), 互 (mutual) and 自 (self), such as 共享 (share), 共建 (build together),
互利 (mutual benefit), 互补 (complementary), 自信 (self-confidence) and 自卫 (self-defence),
and on 富裕 in 共同富裕 (common prosperity). It is also slightly positive (mean about 0.1) on
the first token of each document, and clearly negative on the colon of a "Title:" template.

This program predicts those effects and nothing else:
  * a word of sharing or mutual benefit (共享, 互利, ...)     -> 3.0
  * a word of self-reliance (自信, 自负, ...)                 -> 1.5
  * a Chinese token right after a token ending in 共, 互, 自   -> 0.6, 0.8, 0.4
  * the first token of a document                            -> 0.11
  * the colon right after "Title"                            -> -0.64
  * everything else                                          -> 0

It reads the current token, the one before it, and the document labels. Its variance
explained is small (about 0.04 on eval): most of the component's variance is diffuse
small activations on ordinary tokens, which this short program does not capture.
"""

READS = ()

# Words of sharing and mutual benefit: the component's strongest responses.
SHARING_WORDS = {
    "共享", "共建", "共赢", "共识", "共进", "共度", "共济", "互利", "互补", "互通",
    "互助", "互惠", "互信", "互鉴", "互动", "富裕", "资源共享",
}
# Words of self-reliance.
SELF_WORDS = {"自信", "自负", "自律", "自制", "自尊", "自带", "自备", "自立"}
# Bound morphemes that open a compound; the next character takes their response.
OPENERS = {"共": 0.6, "互": 0.8, "自": 0.4}


def is_cjk(text):
    return len(text) > 0 and all("一" <= ch <= "鿿" for ch in text)


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    docs = prefix.document_ids
    if prefix.position == 0 or docs[-1] != docs[-2]:
        return None, 0.11  # first token of a document
    cur = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    prev = prefix.token_strings[-2]
    if cur == ":" and prev.endswith("Title"):
        return None, -0.64
    if not is_cjk(cur):
        return None, 0.0
    if cur in SHARING_WORDS:
        return None, 3.0
    if cur in SELF_WORDS:
        return None, 1.5
    if prev and prev[-1] in OPENERS:
        return None, OPENERS[prev[-1]]
    return None, 0.0

"""Layer 1 MLP down-projection, component 1469.

What it does: this component fires on the Greek letter epsilon. It is strongest
when the epsilon is the second letter of a word, i.e. it directly follows a
lowercase Greek letter token (ε, έ, Ε). How strong depends on the letter before
it: after ρ, χ, λ, ι, ν, γ, π, φ it fires hard; after τ, δ, μ it fires weakly.
An epsilon that starts a word (after a space or punctuation) gives almost nothing.

It also fires on a few other kinds of token seen in the data: runs of
non-breaking spaces (padding), long dot leaders, long runs of plain spaces,
Tamil letters, and the NUL character. Every other token is predicted as 0.

The values are rough averages of the real activation for each case, read off
training text. The per-letter table is the one part that is a list of letters
rather than a rule; without it, the epsilon case is predicted at a single value.
"""

READS = ()

# Mean activation of the epsilon in a word, by the lowercase Greek letter before it.
PREV_LETTER = {"ρ": 10, "χ": 7.4, "λ": 7.0, "ι": 6.5, "γ": 5.5, "ν": 6.0, "π": 5.6, "φ": 6.0,
               "σ": 4.3, "θ": 4.0, "ζ": 3.6, "κ": 3.2, "β": 3.8, "ο": 4.0,
               "τ": 2.4, "δ": 2.3, "μ": 2.1}
# Each form of epsilon relative to the table above.
EPSILON_FORMS = {"ε": 1.0, "έ": 1.15, "Ε": 0.7}
DEFAULT_PREV = 4.5


def is_lower_greek(ch):
    return ("α" <= ch <= "ω") or ("ἀ" <= ch <= "῿")


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    tok = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    prev = prefix.token_strings[-2] if len(prefix) > 1 else ""
    # Epsilon inside a Greek word.
    if tok in EPSILON_FORMS and prev and is_lower_greek(prev[-1]):
        return None, EPSILON_FORMS[tok] * PREV_LETTER.get(prev, DEFAULT_PREV)
    # Epsilon after a space, which starts a word.
    if tok == " ε":
        return None, 1.4
    # NUL character.
    if tok == "\x00":
        return None, 1.8
    # Runs of non-breaking spaces (padding).
    if len(tok) >= 8 and " " in tok and set(tok) <= {" ", " "}:
        return None, 5.0
    # Long dot leaders.
    if len(tok) >= 16 and set(tok) <= {".", " "} and "." in tok:
        return None, 3.5
    # Long runs of plain spaces.
    if len(tok) >= 64 and set(tok) <= {" "}:
        return None, 3.0
    # Tamil letters.
    if any("஀" <= c <= "௿" for c in tok):
        return None, 3.0
    return None, 0.0

"""Traceback " line" detector for layers.1.mlp.down_proj:1470.

The component is a rank-one piece of the layer-1 MLP output. Almost all of its
activation is small, diffuse noise (its std is about 0.05) that no simple rule
captures. Its one clear job is in Python tracebacks: it fires on the word
" line" in a frame such as

    File "/usr/lib/python3/site-packages/foo/bar.py", line 42, in <module>

strongly (about 0.8) when the filename ends in ".py" (the token `",` comes
right before), and more weakly (about 0.3) when the filename is a pseudo-file
such as `File "<string>", line 7` (the token `>",` comes right before).
Everywhere else it predicts 0.

The program is stateless: it looks only at the newest token and the one before.
"""

READS = ()


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    toks = prefix.token_strings
    value = 0.0
    if len(toks) >= 2 and toks[-1] == " line":
        if toks[-2] == '",':
            value = 0.8
        elif toks[-2] == '>",':
            value = 0.3
    return None, value

"""layers.1.mlp.down_proj:1471: a "first token of a text" detector.

What it does: this component is almost silent inside a text. It speaks only at the
first token of a document segment, the token with no earlier context: position 0 of
a packed row, or the first token after <|endoftext|>. There the model's attention can
see nothing but the token itself, so the component's value is set by which kind of
token it is (the value is the same every time that token starts a segment):

  - whitespace, digits and common function words ("the", "to", "with") go negative;
  - non-Latin scripts (CJK, Cyrillic) and longer capitalised words or code/label
    fragments go positive, most of all non-Latin ones;
  - short punctuation goes negative; other short tokens sit near zero.

Everywhere else it predicts 0.

This is a rough, readable approximation. The true value depends on each token
individually; these few word classes explain only part of the variance.
"""

READS = ()

FUNCTION_WORDS = frozenset(
    """the of to and a an in is it that for with was on as by be at or this are from
    not but have he she they we you i his her its their which who has had were been
    will would can could should may there these those then than so if when what all
    any more one also about into over after before up out no just only other some
    such""".split()
)


def start_value(token: str) -> float:
    """Mean activation at a segment's first token, for a token of this kind."""
    text = token.strip()
    if not text or text.isdigit() or text.lower() in FUNCTION_WORDS:
        return -0.6
    if any("一" <= ch <= "鿿" for ch in text):  # CJK ideographs
        return 1.5
    if any("Ѐ" <= ch <= "ӿ" for ch in text):  # Cyrillic
        return 2.1
    if any(ord(ch) > 127 for ch in text):  # other non-Latin scripts
        return 1.2
    short = len(text) <= 2
    if text[0].isupper():  # capitalised word
        return 0.3 if short else 1.3
    if text.isalpha():  # lowercase word
        return 0.25 if short else 0.15
    return -0.5 if short else 1.0  # punctuation, code, labels


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    position = prefix.position
    starts_segment = position == 0 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]
    if not starts_segment:
        return None, 0.0
    return None, start_value(prefix.token_strings[-1])
